ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation, all UBOs and managers must be screened against the French ministries' national sanctions database (Fichel), the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, and, because USD settlement is available, the OFAC SDN list. PEP status is checked using a robust AML database and sources of wealth; enhanced due diligence is mandatory if a PEP, family member or close associate is identified, under CMF Articles L.561-10-1 and L.561-10-2, including senior foreign officials and domestic politically exposed persons in high-risk functions. Negative media and adverse legal event searches must be finalised before the bank account opening.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises (https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) operated by INPI; company name verification against the RCS/NATIONAL SIRENE database through Infogreffe (www.infogreffe.fr).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name may be in any language but must be expressed in Latin characters for entry in the French trade registry; non-Latin names are rejected and must be transliterated. The name must comply with Article R.123-10 of the Code de commerce, which prohibits names that are contrary to public order or misleading about the company's activity; the suffix 'SARL' or 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' must appear in all corporate communications. A foreign-language name must not use regulated words without prior authorisation.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: République française / Président de la République / Ministre — prior ministerial authorisation required for any official-state reference
Banque / bank / crédit — requires ACPR banking licence and prior authorisation
Assurance / mutuelle — requires ACPR and statutory insurance authorisation
Fondation or fonds — requires prior regulatory approval and special statutory form
Chambre de commerce et d'industrie (CCI) / Ordre / Syndicat — statutory reserved names
Terms suggesting a main activity not covered by ISIC 4638 such as 'boucherie', 'pharmacie' or food-safety regulated denominations — prior administrative authorisation required
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: When the Guichet unique returns a name rejection, the applicant should first file a reasoned 'recours gracieux' through the INPI helpdesk within 15 calendar days of rejection, attaching the rejection notification and the desired RCS availability search. If the rejection is upheld or remains silent, a hierarchical appeal should be lodged with the Bureau des entreprises, Ministère de la Justice, within 30 days, and further review may be initiated before the competent tribunal judiciaire within the applicable two-month administrative-litigation window. A reservation may be extended for one further 30-day period by filing a renewal before expiry; no extension is available after expiration without a new filing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A SARL may validly use an approved commercial domiciliation provider's address as its registered office in France under Article L.123-11-2 of the Code de commerce; this is sufficient for registration and correspondence, but it must not be a formless 'virtual provider' with no real administrative basis. Because the company is engaged in food and HORECA supply, a dedicated commercial substance address for storage, customs clearance, invoicing and book-keeping is recommended to avoid French tax residence or permanent-establishment inquiries.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 10-15% per fiscal year for a newly incorporated SARL with a standard domiciliation address; the probability rises to 25-35% if DGCCRF or French Customs inspect food products, imported dehydrated vegetables or VAT/customs declarations. A pure virtual-registered-officer arrangement triggers targeted inspection and tax residence review at an assessed elevated probability of 35%.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Code de commerce (French Commercial Code), Book II, Articles L.210-1 et seq. and L.223-1 to L.223-42 (Société à Responsabilité Limitée - SARL)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) through the Guichet Unique / Infogreffe portal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts (Articles of Association) together with the M0 (or Cerfa) incorporation filing form and supporting exhibits
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for SARL; capital is freely set in the Statuts. If composed of cash contributions, all shares must be fully subscribed and at least 10% of cash contributions paid-up at incorporation; unblocking of the escrowed funds occurs upon registration. In-kind contributions must be fully paid-up at constitution.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: The initial member subscribes to one hundred shares, nominal value one euro each, representing the entire share capital; such shares are fully subscribed and fully paid by bank transfer to the Company's blocked account. RESOLVED: The registered office is established at [address] as stated in the Statuts; the Manager is authorized to utilize this address for all corporate registrations. RESOLVED: The Manager of the Company is appointed as first Manager; he/she receives full authority to open bank accounts, sign any registration or licensing documents, and complete all formalities before the Commercial Court Registry and public authorities. RESOLVED: The Manager shall undertake all administrative and legal steps for the Company's formation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve corporate name and confirm availability
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) via inpi.fr; verification against the RCS database
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary name availability search on Infogreffe/INPI. File a name reservation request by completing the online form and paying the applicable fee. If no conflicting name is found, the reservation is recorded and used later in the incorporation filing.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of reservation fee
Power of attorney if filed by agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to conflict, modify the proposed name and re-file. The initial fee may be credited or forfeited depending on the commercial registry's schedule.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft, sign and deposit capital and articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary (optional but recommended) or the attorneys acting for the subscriber; statutory capital deposit to a blocked account held by a bank or notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Association (Statuts) specifying the corporate object, registered office, subscribed capital, share distribution, management structure and governance rules. Open a temporary block account and transfer the cash portion of the capital. Obtain a capital deposit certificate from the bank or notary. All members must sign the Statuts, either privately or through a notarial deed.
required_dossiers: Identity documents and declarations of the subscriber/member
CV or manager declaration if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to open the blocked account due to incomplete documents, correct the documents and reapply. If the Statuts are defective, revise the draft and re-sign, then obtain a new deposit certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish legal notice in an official gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'Annonces Légales – approved official publication outlet designated by the Prefecture
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Insert a notice of the incorporation in an authorized official gazette (JAL) stating the SARL's corporate name, registered office address, corporate purpose, capital amount, association management details, and the registration registry where the filing will be made. Obtain the attesting publication receipt (attestation de parution).
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of the publication fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL requests amendments, submit a revised notice and incur a new publication fee; notarized articles must be identical to the published details.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit incorporation dossier to the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises operated by Infogreffe, transmitted to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the standardized incorporation form (Cerfa M0), upload the signed Statuts, the JAL publication receipt, the capital deposit certificate, and the identity declarations. Select the RCS filing request and pay the filing fee. Electronically sign the submission. The Guichet Unique forwards the file to the Commercial Court Registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a query (demande de régularisation), upload the requested supplementary documents or modifications within the prescribed deadline. If rejection is final, rectify the deficiencies and submit a fresh application with a new fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain the RCS registration certificate (extrait K-bis)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once approved, the Registry will enter the company in the Register du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) and issue the official extract (extrait K-bis). The certificate includes the company's registration number (SIREN), legal form, registered office, share capital, managers, and the assigned NAF code. A free electronic copy is available from Infogreffe.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the K-bis is delayed beyond the statutory period, contact the Registry directly with the dossier reference; if the certificate contains errors, apply for rectification through the Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: URSSAF, Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFIP), local municipal administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the SIREN registration, the Guichet Unique automatically notifies tax and social security authorities for establishment of the company identification file. Obtain a company SIRET number and tax registration. Register the managing officer with social security and apply for any optional permits or operating certificates as needed for the actual business address (e.g., business premises authorization, if a shop or warehouse is used).
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If URSSAF or DGFIP issues a discrepancy inquiry, provide the official registration extract and clarify the corporate legal status. If the local prefecture imposes additional requirements, complete the required administrative declarations within the argued deadline.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Régionale de l'Économie, de l'Emploi, du Travail et des Solidarités (DREETS) – applicable only for industrial/processing undertakings; not applicable for this pure wholesale trading operation
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Unclassified wholesale trading activity (négociant / commerce de gros) is not subject to a dedicated operating licence under commercial law; a valid K-bis registration and normal business registration suffice.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL) / Ministère de la Transition écologique
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not required – exempt as the activity is wholesale trading of dehydrated vegetables and spices without processing, manufacturing, or significant emissions.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Given the absence of manufacturing processes, no industrial discharge, VOC, or waste-treatment thresholds are triggered. The company, when using warehouses, must comply with general local urbanism and waste-management obligations (ordinary commercial waste disposal via a licensed waste collector).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For an office/warehouse-only trading company, civil defense clearance is limited to compliance with the municipal fire-safety, building and workplace health codes at the leased premises. Prior to occupancy, obtain an attestation de conformité from the property owner and verify that the building's fire-safety and evacuation standards meet the requirements for commercial premises. No dedicated industrial clearance is required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), administered through the relevant Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE). The principal portal is impots.gouv.fr. Business formation and registration data are filed through the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI), while INSEE issues the SIREN and SIRET identifiers.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SARL is formed through the Guichet unique managed by INPI. The filing includes constitutional documents, registered office evidence, beneficial-owner information, management identification, business activity, and, where applicable, establishment and customs information. Following registration, INSEE issues the SIREN and establishment-specific SIRET. The competent SIE assigns the French intra-Community VAT number, generally formatted as FR plus a two-character control key and the nine-digit SIREN. The entity must activate its professional account on impots.gouv.fr and file the applicable VAT registration or option forms. A foreign entity without a French establishment applies to the Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères for a French VAT number when it carries out transactions for which France has taxing jurisdiction. A non-EU entity generally must appoint an accredited French fiscal representative unless an applicable statutory exemption applies; EU-established businesses are generally not required to appoint one. VAT registration does not by itself create a French permanent establishment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SARL is generally subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) by default. A family SARL meeting statutory conditions may elect income-tax treatment, and a qualifying newly formed SARL may elect temporary income-tax treatment for up to five financial years, subject to eligibility, shareholder, turnover, employee, and activity conditions. The election is not a United States-style check-the-box election and is subject to notification and timing requirements. French anti-hybrid-mismatch rules implement the EU ATAD framework and may deny deductions, include income, or impose other corrective treatment for hybrid mismatches; they do not provide a general elective hybrid classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, or VAT), supplemented by customs import VAT and selected excise and local indirect taxes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: France does not provide a single universal VAT-registration threshold for all taxable businesses. The French VAT franchise regime generally permits eligible established businesses to remain outside VAT collection while annual domestic turnover does not exceed approximately EUR 85,000 for supplies of goods and specified commercial activities or EUR 37,500 for services, subject to statutory annual threshold and tolerance rules. Businesses exceeding the applicable limits, opting for VAT, importing goods, making taxable intra-Community transactions, or carrying out transactions requiring immediate registration may need VAT registration regardless of those franchise thresholds. The EU-wide EUR 10,000 threshold is relevant principally to certain intra-Community distance sales and electronically supplied, telecommunications, and broadcasting services, not to ordinary domestic wholesale exports.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France does not currently operate universal real-time VAT invoice clearance or mandatory digital stamping for all private-sector invoices. The e-invoicing reform requires all French-established businesses to be able to receive electronic invoices from 1 September 2026. Mandatory issuance begins on 1 September 2026 for large and mid-sized enterprises and on 1 September 2027 for small and micro-enterprises, subject to legally applicable implementation rules. Electronic invoices must use an approved platform or public platform architecture and structured or hybrid formats. Transaction and payment data reporting (e-reporting) will apply to specified business-to-consumer, cross-border, and payment transactions. Invoices to French public-sector customers are handled through Chorus Pro. Export invoices generally remain outside the domestic B2B e-invoicing scope where the transaction is outside the French domestic reporting perimeter, but customs and VAT evidence must be retained.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from France to destinations outside the European Union may be invoiced without French VAT under Article 262 of the French Tax Code if the goods are dispatched or transported outside the EU and the exporter can prove both the export transaction and exit from the EU customs territory. The exporter must be identified for VAT purposes where required and retain a customs export declaration, exit confirmation, commercial invoice, transport evidence, and transaction records. Intra-Community supplies of goods may be exempt from French VAT where the customer is VAT-identified in another EU Member State, the goods are transported from France to that Member State, and the supplier retains the required VAT-number and transport evidence. Services supplied to a business customer established outside France are generally taxed according to place-of-supply rules and may be outside the scope of French VAT rather than technically zero-rated; specific exceptions apply. Input VAT refunds require valid invoices, import documents, customs records, and evidence that the costs relate to taxable business activities.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic export customs declaration filed through the applicable French customs system, including the Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Customs release and exit results, such as the electronic export exit confirmation or equivalent proof of exit
Commercial invoice identifying the exporter, consignee, goods, value, delivery terms, and VAT treatment
Packing list and product description, including quantities, weights, and commodity classification
Bill of lading, airway bill, CMR consignment note, or equivalent transport document
Purchase order, sales contract, delivery evidence, and customer account records
Proof of transport and destination outside the European Union
Export permits, sanitary or phytosanitary documents, certificates of origin, and product-specific documents where applicable to dehydrated vegetables or spices
Evidence of payment or bank settlement where commercially available; an inward remittance certificate is not a general French statutory prerequisite for export VAT exemption
For intra-Community supplies rather than third-country exports, the customer's valid EU VAT identification number and evidence of transport to the other Member State
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France has no general statutory 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export proceeds. Export VAT exemption may be reassessed if customs exit evidence, transport proof, customer identification, invoices, or transaction records are missing, inconsistent, or unreliable. The reassessed VAT may include late-payment interest generally calculated at 0.20% per month, together with tax penalties. Common penalty levels include 10% for late or omitted filing, 40% for deliberate non-compliance, and up to 80% for fraudulent activity or abusive concealment, subject to statutory conditions and procedural safeguards. Customs breaches may additionally trigger duty and import-VAT assessments, customs penalties, seizure, or forfeiture. Serious intentional tax fraud may result in criminal prosecution and imprisonment or fines for responsible individuals, with separate or increased sanctions potentially applicable to legal entities. Refunds or input-VAT credits obtained on the basis of fraudulent or unsupported export claims may be clawed back with interest and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), in statistical cooperation with the Direction Générale du Trésor (General Directorate of the Treasury, French Ministry of the Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty); prudential and AML supervision delegated to the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution). France has no separate foreign-exchange control administration; exchange-control authority is exercised through the Banque de France balance-of-payments (BOP) regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a euro-area Member State with full current-account and capital-account convertibility under Articles 63-65 TFEU, Council Directive 88/361/EEC, and the French Code monétaire et financier. The euro is freely convertible without surrender rules, FX licensing, or profit-remittance quotas. A French SARL may invoice in EUR or any foreign currency and may transfer dividends, repayment of shareholder loans, and trade payments freely through authorized banking channels. The only practical hurdles for profit remittance to non-resident shareholders are standard AML/KYC due diligence, the obligation to prove distributable profits per Article L232-11 of the French Code de commerce, and, where applicable, proof of tax-residence for withholding-tax treaty relief; no FX law obstacle exists.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender obligation and no mandatory conversion ratio. Export receipts may be retained in original currency, held in any foreign-currency account, converted to EUR, or used to settle external payables without authorization. The relevant obligations are: (i) statistical reporting to the Banque de France, via the receiving/sending bank, for every cross-border payment exceeding €12,500 (BOP reporting), classified under merchandise trade and direct investment categories; (ii) preservation of underlying export documentation (commercial invoices, packing lists, customs declarations, transport documents) for ten years under commercial law; (iii) compliance with EU/VAT rules on physical export declaration (EORI registration and DTI/SAD customs filings); there is no fixed timeline or surrender ratio.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: MEDIUM. Cross-border digital EMIs (e-money institutions authorized in Luxembourg, Ireland, Lithuania, or other EU states and validly passported through the ACPR under PSD2) can reliably support the SARL's operating treasury — collection of export proceeds, TT/Wire supplier disbursements, multicurrency account balances, and basic FX conversion. Legal constraints: (1) the French banking monopoly in Article L511-1 of the Code monétaire et financier reserves deposit-taking and credit operations to licensed credit institutions, so an EMI cannot grant credit or issue commercial letters of credit; (2) under Articles L526-1 to L526-34, the EMI must validly hold a French or passported EU license and an ACPR-registered agent arrangement to execute French payments; (3) if the EMI issues a non-French IBAN that is not accepted by French public administrations, treasury friction may arise; (4) LCs under UCP600 are impossible through a pure EMI, requiring a Tier-1 bank or a licensed bank partner. Overall: adequate for TT/Wire clearing, inadequate as sole trade-finance rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a SARL with non-resident shareholders and directors, Tier-1 French banks overwhelmingly mandate a face-to-face meeting: the gérant (legal representative) must attend a branch interview with original passports, and any ultimate beneficial owner holding more than 25% must provide notarised identification or attend in person. Remote video identification is legally recognised (Article R561-5-1 of the Code monétaire et financier) and accepted on a discretionary basis by most major banks for low-risk structures, subject to an escalated compliance review. Where the account is opened for capital-escrow purposes or involves cross-border shareholder injections, physical presence of at least one director is effectively mandatory. The bank will verify the RBE (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) filing at INPI, the original Kbis extract issued within three months, and the SARL's articles.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ultimate beneficial ownership chain or UBO registration not yet filed in the RBE registry
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully submitted RBE filing with INPI receipt; Kbis extract issued within 3 months; certified corporate org chart showing all intermediate entities; certified passport copies of the gérant and all >25% UBOs; proof of residential address for each UBO; notarised shareholder register; board/minutes resolution approving account opening; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements; if foreign corporate shareholders exist, certified constitutional documents and tax residence certificates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border trade corridor involving high-risk or emerging-market commodity counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed supply/purchase contracts (contrats de vente/achat) with counterparties; proforma and final commercial invoices with INCOTERMS; packing lists; full-set transport documents (B/L or AWB); customs export declarations (Déclaration d'Échanges de Biens / SAD/CAD); certificates of origin; independent third-party inspection reports (SGS, Intertek, or similar); phytosanitary certificate where the destination regime requires; Certificate of Analysis for dehydrated garlic and chili pepper quality; EU customs status documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction velocity or aggregates inconsistent with the declared SARL capital base and low-risk ISIC classification
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan and projected cash-flow model; capital contribution deposit certificate (certificat de dépôt des fonds) from the escrow bank; audited or accountant-certified financial statements of the SARL and shareholder; order book and pipeline contracts; historical bank references; explanatory memorandum covering invoice timing, settlement terms, payment splits, and any third-party payment instructions; ACPR-compliant source-of-funds justification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discrepancy between declared activity (wholesale of dehydrated vegetables/spices) and actual documentary profile of payments
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Kbis extract; EORI registration and French VAT certificate; warehousing or toll-processing agreements; supplier identity and licences; purchaser identity and EU/import-side references; quality and food-safety compliance certificates (HACCP, ISO-22000 where applicable); rapid-alert and health certificates for food imports; independent laboratory reports on the goods; bank-to-bank reference request; confirmatory legal opinion that the activity is non-licenced under French rules.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically Exposed Person (PEP) flag or negative media/sanctions screening hit on a shareholder, director, or trading counterparty
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formal PEP declarations signed by each director and UBO; negative media report from a reputable due-diligence provider; consolidated EU financial sanctions list screening report; OFAC non-binding but bank-policy screening where relevant; certified identification and proof of political-neutral employment or business history; source-of-wealth documentation; senior compliance sign-off letter from the bank's AML committee where the relationship is approved on enhanced due diligence.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity subscriptions or shareholder advances must be remitted to the SARL's French operational account: for EUR flows, use SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) with the IBAN and BIC of the French bank; for non-EUR flows, use SWIFT MT103 with Field 50K (ordering customer), Field 59 (beneficiary SARL, BIC/IBAN), and Field 70 Remittance Information clearly stating 'Apport en capital — augmentation de capital — SARL [Name]' or 'Compte courant d'associé' for shareholder loans. France applies no exchange-control prior approval; the only regulatory layer is the Banque de France balance-of-payments statistical declaration, executed by the beneficiary bank for any cross-border credit above €12,500, classified under BOP direct-investment categories. The receiving bank will demand: the capital-increase deed (décision de l'associé unique/procès-verbal), a deposit certificate from the escrow bank or notary, the acte de dépôt de fonds, updated Kbis, RBE confirmation, source-of-funds bank statements of the subscribing shareholder, and identity documents of the legal representatives. All funds must flow through the same banking channel as the declared UBO structure.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements should be executed through the following clearing rails: (1) SEPA Credit Transfer (SEPA CT) for EUR payments to EU suppliers using IBAN/BIC with Field 70 invoice references; (2) SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfer for non-EUR suppliers, quoting the commercial invoice number, contract reference, and INCOTERMS in Field 70, with the SARL as ordering party and any necessary correspondent-bank instructions in Field 72B; (3) irrevocable documentary Letters of Credit (Commercial LCs) governed by ICC UCP600, issued or received through French banks and transmitted by SWIFT MT700, with confirmation through correspondents in the seller's jurisdiction; (4) standby LCs and documentary collection (DP/DA) as supplements. The document set required under LCs for dehydrated garlic flakes and chili pepper exports must include: commercial invoice signed in triplicate, full-set clean on-board bill of lading or air waybill, packing list, certificate of origin (EUR.1 or Form A as applicable), phytosanitary certificate where required by the importing country, quality and weight certificates, certificate of analysis for the dehydrated vegetable/spice specification, and any customs export declarations. All disbursements remain subject to EU restrictive-measures/sanctions screening, AML transaction monitoring, and Banque de France BOP reporting thresholds; full supporting trade documents must be conserved for ten years.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD deliverable FX forwards (change à terme) up to 12-month tenors, supported by underlying export receivables or import payables
FX swaps (swap de change) for rolling short-term hedging and liquidity management across currencies
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted-deliverability currencies where offshore hedging is required (e.g., certain Asian or African currencies)
Cross-currency swaps for multi-year balance-sheet or P&L exposure in significant invoice currencies
Plain-vanilla FX options and combos (zero-cost collars) subject to ISDA/CMCE master agreement and ACPR-compliant documentation
Currency forwards embedded in trade-finance products (LC discounting and confirmed LC payables) provided the hedging intent is documented

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval and filing of annual accounts, management report, and related resolutions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Registry of Enterprises through the INPI single window, with registration at the competent Commercial Court Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders must approve the accounts within six months after the financial year-end. Filing is due within one month after approval, or within two months after approval when filed electronically.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-ordered filing injunctions and daily coercive fines may apply. Late or omitted filing may result in a fine of approximately EUR 1,500, increasing to approximately EUR 3,000 for repeat breaches. There is no automatic strike-off solely on a fixed annual deadline; administrative removal may follow formal notice and failure to regularize, generally after a notice period of approximately three months.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return and annual tax package
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Directorate General of Public Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year taxpayer, generally by the second business day after 1 May of the following year. For a non-calendar financial year, generally within three months after year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing generally attracts a 10% surcharge, increased penalties in specified circumstances, and late-payment interest generally calculated at 0.20% per month, subject to statutory exceptions and adjustments.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate property tax filing and payment, where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Directorate General of Public Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Corporate property tax is generally payable by 15 December. The initial property declaration and subsequent changes follow separate statutory deadlines.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment may trigger a 5% surcharge and late-payment interest. This is a tax liability rather than a company-law renewal fee and does not itself create an automatic strike-off deadline.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership information update, if ownership or control details change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Registry of Enterprises through the INPI single window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No annual confirmation filing is required solely because a new year begins. Changes to beneficial ownership information generally must be reported within 30 days.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or inaccurate filing may result in criminal penalties, registry restrictions, and court-ordered compliance. There is no automatic annual strike-off rule for a missing confirmation; removal or other registry action may follow formal notice and non-regularization.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally mandatory for a SARL exceeding at least two of three thresholds at the financial year-end: EUR 5 million total balance sheet, EUR 10 million net turnover excluding tax, and an average of 50 employees. Additional group-company rules and shareholder or court appointment rights may apply.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP under the French Accounting Standards Authority regulations applies to standalone statutory accounts. IFRS is generally optional for standalone accounts and principally relevant to consolidated accounts where applicable.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not require an annual beneficial ownership confirmation for unchanged ownership. The SARL must maintain accurate beneficial ownership data and file an amendment within 30 days of any change in ownership, control, or identifying information. Share transfers must also be documented and reflected in the company records and registry filings where required.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of shareholders or partners and supporting share-transfer instruments
Register of management and shareholder resolutions and minutes
Annual accounts, management reports, and approval documentation
Beneficial ownership documentation and filed declarations

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 325-1,300 per year, depending on location, mail handling, and service scope
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 2,200-8,000 per year for a small SARL subject to statutory audit, depending on transaction volume, group complexity, and reporting requirements

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard French corporate income tax rate, CGI art. 219, applicable from 1 January 2022); reduced rate of 15% applies to the first EUR 42,000 of taxable profit for qualifying SMEs (turnover below EUR 10 million and fully paid-up capital); a 3.3% social surcharge applies only where the annual income tax exceeds EUR 763,000.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate on the first EUR 42,000 of profit for small enterprises (CGI art. 219-I-b); French territoriality principle limits taxation to profits realized or attributable to French operations, so export margins on dehydrated garlic flakes and chili pepper are taxable in France only where management and risk-taking occur in France; availability of the Research Tax Credit (CIR) for qualifying R&D on dehydration processes and the incentives for green or energy-efficient equipment; no statutory tax holidays exist in France; a 50% deduction is available for qualifying innovation-related profits under the IP box regime when patents or equivalent IP are licensed.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: French corporate income tax return Form No. 2135-SD ('Déclaration de résultats'), supplemented by the balance-sheet annexes of the 2050-series 'liasse fiscale'; submitted electronically through the Impôt Gouverneur Professional portal ('Gérer mon compte professionnel' on impots.gouv.fr) using EFI/EDI encrypted filing channels.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual filing of the 2135-SD final return, supplemented by four mandatory quarterly advance payments of corporate income tax (acomptes) due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December; a balancing payment is due with the final annual return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending on 31 December, the 2135-SD declaration must be filed no later than the second business day following 1 May of the following year; for fiscal years ending on any other date, filing is due within three months of the fiscal year-end plus two business days; e-filing remains mandatory for all corporations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the French SARL exactly as registered in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact declared French legal name; do not use a trade name, foreign translation or group brand; mismatches between the tax return, RCS extract and bank beneficiary name used on Swift LC/TT instructions will trigger bank and tax administration review.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Nine-digit French company identification number issued by the INSEE.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Quote the SIREN as stated in the statutory registration; the SARL must also disclose the APE code (equivalent of ISIC 4638) corresponding to the dehydrated-vegetable and spices wholesale trade; a missing or inconsistent APE code may trigger a tax-audit preliminary questionnaire.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting profit or loss for the fiscal year before corporate income tax, extracted from the statutory annual accounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the accounting result with the 2053 balance sheet and 2052 income statement; for the French export structure, verify that all foreign exchange gains or losses under TT/Wire receipts and LC settlements are booked; under the French territoriality rule, foreign permanent-establishment income is excluded only if a PE is effectively demonstrated outside France.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable result after extra-accounting adjustments (réintégrations and déductions), including disallowed expenses, depreciation corrections, and prior-year loss offsets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For the SARL owned by a non-resident parent, confirm that all transactions with related overseas entities are priced at arm's length and that no hidden profit-shifting has occurred; the tax administration may request a detailed reconciliation demonstrating the margins on exported dehydrated vegetables and spices.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or failure to file triggers an automatic increase of 10% of the assessed corporate income tax (CGI art. 1728); where the company does not respond within 30 days after a formal notice, the penalty rises to 40%; deliberate misstatement or concealment triggers 40% (art. 1729) and fraud or abuse of law triggers 80% (art. 1729-0 A); late payments carry monthly late-payment interest of 0.20%; enforcement includes forced collection, attachment of bank accounts and publication of a lien.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% domestic French withholding tax (CGI art. 119 bis) on dividend distributions to non-French corporate shareholders that do not qualify for the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive; 30% flat withholding for distributions to non-resident individuals (12.8% income tax plus 17.2% social levies); 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where the EU/EEA corporate shareholder holds directly at least 5% of the SARL's capital for two consecutive years; under the France-China DTA the rate may be reduced to 10% for a corporate shareholder holding at least 25% of the share capital, subject to beneficial ownership evidence.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a reduced DTA rate, the foreign shareholder must obtain an official tax residence certificate (TRC / attestation de résidence fiscale) from its home tax authority for the calendar year of the distribution; before making the distribution, the foreign beneficiary must submit Form 5000 (application for treaty benefits) and Form 5001 (tax residence certificate) to the French withholding agent or the local tax office (SIE); where withholding has been levied at the domestic rate, a refund claim must be filed with the tax office competent for the payer no later than 31 December of the second year following the year the withholding was applied; supporting files must include the DTA article relied upon, the shareholding chain, length of holding, and the beneficial-ownership analysis; because the target export structure receives Swift LC/TT proceeds into the French SARL, no French withholding tax arises on inbound receipts by the company.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid by the French SARL to non-residents for intellectual property or technical services are subject to a domestic French withholding tax of 33.33% (CGI art. 182 B); this is reduced to 0% under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive where the EU/EEA creditor is an associated company holding at least 25% of the French payer for an uninterrupted period of two years; treaty rates commonly range from 0% to 10%, with the France-China DTA generally allowing 10% on royalties; interest paid by the French SARL to foreign banks or suppliers under ordinary arm's-length Swift LC/TT trade financing is not subject to any French withholding tax, provided the creditor is not resident in a privileged-tax jurisdiction; abusive excessive interest paid to a related party is recharacterized as a hidden distribution and taxed at the statutory dividend WHT rate, so the interest rate must be benchmarked and documented.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 50,000,000 of annual turnover or gross assets and more than 400 employees (CGI art. L13 AA); where the French SARL or the worldwide group to which it belongs exceeds this size, a full Transfer Pricing Documentation package (Master File, Local File and a CbC report where applicable) is mandatory; for the target SARL below the threshold, the tax administration may still issue a specific information request under CGI art. L13 AB requiring proportionate legal, accounting and pricing evidence; local currency is EUR, and contemporaneous year-end pricing documentation for dehydrated garlic flakes and crushed chili pepper margins is essential.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Metropolitan France does not operate an Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime like offshore financial centres; however, French anti-abuse provisions (CGI art. L64 LPF on 'abus de droit'), the beneficial-ownership condition embedded in all French tax treaties, and the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive require the SARL to demonstrate genuine commercial substance in France: a physical office or warehouse lease, a gérant exercising real management decisions in France, employment or subcontracting arrangements for warehousing and logistics, local bank accounts receiving the LC/TT settlements, and board minutes supporting purchase and sale decisions for dehydrated vegetables and spices; absence of such substance allows the administration to disregard the French entity, reattribute its export income to the foreign principal, deny treaty benefits and apply penalties of up to 80%.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission or concealment of export turnover on the 2135-SD return; invoicing dehydrated garlic flakes or chili pepper shipments through an undisclosed foreign conduit bank account; submission of falsified customs documents or destruction of Swift LC/TT evidence during a tax audit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine of up to EUR 500,000 and imprisonment of up to five years under CGI art. 1741; increased to EUR 3,000,000 and seven years for organised fraud; civil re-assessment plus 0.20% monthly interest, with 40% penalty for deliberate concealment and 80% penalty for fraud or abuse of law (CGI art. 1729 and 1729-0 A).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant and signatories may be held jointly and severally liable for the SARL's unpaid corporate income tax, VAT and social contributions under CGI art. L266 LPF where they organised the concealment; courts may impose an interdiction de gérer, an interdiction du territoire français, attachment of personal assets, and a ban on managing any French company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SARL exclusively as a paper vehicle with no office, no employees, no warehouse, no local decision-making, and all commercial control exercised from abroad; failure to maintain a real economic presence in France while routing high-value export contracts through the entity solely to obtain treaty benefits or avoid taxation in the home state.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Invocation of the abuse-of-law procedure (CGI art. L64 LPF) permits the tax administration to disregard the artificial entity, recharacterize the contracts and reattribute the export income to the truly controlling foreign party; an 80% penalty applies where the artificiality is deliberate (CGI art. 1729-0 A); the Registry may also strike the company off the RCS.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly maintain a fictitious structure are jointly liable for all taxes evaded (CGI art. L266 LPF); commercial courts may impose faillite personnelle, an interdiction de gérer, seizure of personal bank accounts, and a travel ban; criminal prosecution for fraud and false statements may lead to imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving export proceeds in cash or through unlicensed virtual or non-EU personal accounts outside the declared Swift LC/TT banking rails; failing to declare the beneficial owner (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs) at the RCS; structuring transactions to avoid thresholds for automatic bank reporting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Code monétaire et financier art. L465-1: imprisonment of up to five years and a fine of EUR 375,000; organised-money-laundering aggravating circumstance: seven years and EUR 750,000; additional EUR 30,000 fine for failure to file the beneficial-owner declaration; confiscation of laundered proceeds is mandatory.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant is criminally prosecutable as an officer of a legal person where the SARL was knowingly used to launder the proceeds of export transactions; the court may order provisional freezing of personal and corporate assets, issue an interdiction de gérer, impose a travel ban, and deliver international rogatory letters to attach accounts in foreign bank branches.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Deficiencies and Margin Erosion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Where the French SARL belongs to a group with a foreign parent and the group exceeds the documentation thresholds: failure to produce the Master File, Local File or CbC report upon lawful audit demand; alternatively, pricing the export of dehydrated vegetables and spices to a related offshore distributor at a margin below the French arm's-length range so as to shift profit outside France.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Re-assessment at the arm's-length price under CGI art. L13 AA/AB; refusal to produce the required documentation triggers a penalty of 5% of the re-assessed amounts, with a minimum of EUR 10,000 per missing documentation element (CGI art. 1735 ter); in addition, 40% bad-faith penalties and 0.20% monthly late-payment interest accrue; no corresponding foreign tax credit is granted where the adjusted profit is repatriated.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant who obstructs the tax audit or refuses to produce the documentation commits the offence of opposition to tax control (CGI art. 1746) punishable by a fine of EUR 10,000 to EUR 50,000 and up to five years' imprisonment; in insolvency proceedings, directors may be ordered to bear corporate tax liabilities personally under CGI art. L267 LPF when their imprudence or wrongful acts caused the loss.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying the foreign parent or its affiliates sums denominated as 'management fees', 'advisory fees' or 'royalties' under fabricated or unsigned contracts, without a true service rendered, and without booking a verifiable dividend declaration, thereby circumventing the 25% dividend withholding tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of the payments as constructive dividends: assessment of the 25% withholding tax (or 30% for individuals), reversal of the deduction for the French company, 0.20% monthly late-payment interest, and an additional 40% penalty for deliberate inaccurate declaration; the foreign recipient will be denied treaty relief absent beneficial ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant who approved or signed the irregular payment is personally liable to the tax authority for the withheld amounts not remitted (CGI art. 265 LPF); criminal exposure for abuse of corporate assets (abus de biens sociaux) is also established, carrying up to five years' imprisonment and EUR 375,000 fine, with the director barred from managing commercial entities.
